accuracy.evidence: Matches EYFS/Y1 one-to-one correspondence: one number name per object, no skip/double-count, last number = cardinality of the set.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets double-count, skip, counting gaps, and last-number≠total in lab why() plus adult notes and challenge traps.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab teaches touch-once pairing while saying numbers — distinct from numeral→object build (flagrepnum) and count-to-five naming (flagcount).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner taps each grape once, spots double-count and skip, rebuilds five touches, links last number to how many.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (fast recite, gaps, double OK, colour) are overturned by tap/double/skip/last/idea tasks.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names fast/loud/toys, gaps/onlygaps, fair/two/mustskip/big, nothing/skiplast, plus/colour slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 4–6 wording: short kid lines; one-to-one, skip, double-count named plainly.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches pairing, a mistake to reject, or the last-number rule.

mobile.evidence: Large touch/reset buttons; tap twins for drag; challenge stack usable at phone width; young class.

accessibility.evidence: Tap, double, skip, rebuild, last, idea expose lbtn twins; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK EYFS / National Curriculum Maths Y1: count reliably with one-to-one correspondence
NCETM Early Number: one-to-one correspondence and cardinality (last number principle)
BBC Bitesize KS1 Maths: counting objects carefully
